final_static_definitions: I is the index of curvature; the fixed interval is divided into 4 equal parts (quarters). R_4 is the total (cumulative) number of responses emitted during the interval; R_1, R_2, R_3 are the cumulative numbers of responses emitted by the end of the first, second, and third quarters, respectively. The index equals the normalized area between the cumulative-response curve and the constant-rate diagonal. A constant response rate yields I = 0; positive values indicate positively accelerated (FI-scalloped) responding concentrated near the end of the interval, negative values indicate front-loaded responding. For n = 4 the index is bounded by -3/8 and +3/8 (i.e. ±(n-1)/2n), reaching +3/8 = 0.375 when all responding occurs at the very end of the interval.
final_recursive_definitions: I is the index of curvature; n is the number of equal parts into which the fixed interval is divided; R_n is the total (cumulative) number of responses emitted during the interval; R_i (i = 1, 2, ..., n-1) is the cumulative number of responses emitted by the end of the i-th part. The index equals the normalized area between the cumulative-response curve and the constant-rate diagonal. It is 0 for a constant response rate, increases toward +(n-1)/2n (approaching +0.5 as n increases) as responding becomes concentrated near the end of the interval, and decreases toward -(n-1)/2n for front-loaded responding.

editor_summary: Index 117 (Fry, Kelleher & Cook, 1960, "A mathematical index of performance on fixed-interval schedules"). final_static_equation: P(R \mid t) = 1 - e^{-\lambda t}; P(R \mid t_1) = 1 - e^{-\lambda_1 t_1}; P(R \mid t_2) = 1 - e^{-\lambda_2 t_2}; t_2 > t_1 \frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_2}
final_static_definitions: P(R \mid t) is the cumulative probability that a reinforcer has been set up on a variable-interval (Poisson/random-interval) schedule after an elapsed time t, where t is the time allocated to (or accrued on) an alternative since the relevant resetting event as defined by the paper; \lambda is the scheduled Poisson rate parameter (reinforcement rate). Subscripts 1 and 2 index the two concurrent time-based (VI) alternatives, so \lambda_1, \lambda_2 are their rate parameters and t_1, t_2 the times accrued on each. The 1 - e^{-\lambda t} form applies specifically to the time-based (VI/Poisson) alternatives. The inequality t_2 > t_1(\lambda_1/\lambda_2) is the momentary-maximizing (hill-climbing) decision boundary: it is algebraically equivalent to \lambda_2 t_2 > \lambda_1 t_1, hence to P(R \mid t_2) > P(R \mid t_1), so it specifies the region in which the momentary reinforcement probability on alternative 2 exceeds that on alternative 1 and a momentary-maximizing organism should respond on / switch to alternative 2. The indifference boundary is exact, not an approximation: equating the two momentary probabilities gives e^{-\lambda_1 t_1} = e^{-\lambda_2 t_2}, hence \lambda_1 t_1 = \lambda_2 t_2, so t_2 = t_1(\lambda_1/\lambda_2) is the exact indifference line (the small-\lambda t linear approximation is not needed).
